domain: fictitious agent-evaluation phenomena (invented; chosen so no established real-world term owns them)
note: Ground truth. NEVER readable by any pipeline call. Per-side descriptions are what each community's generator brief contains (its side only, no labels).

a.desc: An agent that succeeds on a multi-step task can fail badly when the evaluation harness randomizes the order in which equivalent tool results are returned between runs, even though the information content is unchanged; the phenomenon is the sharp success-rate drop caused purely by such reordering.

b.desc: An agent that succeeds on a multi-step task can fail badly when the evaluation harness randomizes the order in which equivalent tool results are returned between runs, even though the information content is unchanged; the phenomenon is the sharp success-rate drop caused purely by such reordering.

a.desc: Scoring an agent by the fraction of its intermediate claims (notes and subconclusions written during the task) that are still true when the task ends; a high score means the working notes survive to the end, a low score means most intermediate claims are later contradicted or invalidated.

b.desc: Scoring an agent by the fraction of its intermediate claims (notes and subconclusions written during the task) that are still true when the task ends; a high score means the working notes survive to the end, a low score means most intermediate claims are later contradicted or invalidated.

a.desc: Any systematic change in an agent's behavior caused by the presence of evaluation instrumentation itself — logging wrappers, probes, monitors — whatever the mechanism: timing, prompt contamination, resource contention, or the agent detecting it is being watched.

b.desc: The specific effect where latency added by evaluation instrumentation changes which tool an agent selects — slower instrumented tools get picked less often, so the measured tool-choice distribution is an artifact of the instrumentation's added delay.

a.desc: The specific trick of leaving one required credential or parameter out of the task configuration to see whether the agent notices the gap and asks for it, rather than fabricating a value and continuing.

b.desc: Deliberately withholding part of a task's relevant information from the agent — any part, through any channel — to measure whether and how the agent seeks the missing information rather than proceeding on assumptions.

pairs.core: injecting a controlled fault mid-task to assess recovery behavior

a.desc: Runs where the harness injects controlled tool failures — API errors, timeouts — into the middle of a task on purpose, and the agent is scored on how quickly it recovers and completes; the fault schedule is fixed in the harness, and the headline number is time-to-recovery.
a.residue: fault type = tool failures; scoring = time-to-recovery

b.desc: An assessment where a corrupted data artifact is planted mid-task in the agent's inputs on purpose, and the agent passes only if its final output quarantines or flags the corruption rather than silently propagating it; scoring is binary on containment, not on speed.
b.residue: fault type = corrupted data artifacts; scoring = binary containment

pairs.core: intervening on the agent's scratchpad mid-run to attribute apparent capability to accumulated context versus the model itself

a.desc: Deleting an agent's scratchpad at random checkpoints mid-run and measuring the slope of the performance drop, to estimate how much of its apparent skill lives in the accumulated notes rather than in the model itself.
a.residue: intervention = deletion at random checkpoints; metric = performance-drop slope

b.desc: Replacing an agent's working memory mid-run with a paraphrase produced by a weaker model, then measuring how far the agent's subsequent actions diverge from the unperturbed run; the divergence quantifies how much capability depends on the exact stored wording rather than on the model.
b.residue: intervention = weak-model paraphrase substitution; metric = action divergence

a.desc: Periodically re-running a frozen benchmark suite against a deployed agent to detect silent capability changes after the underlying provider model is updated; the comparison is this period's scores against the frozen baseline.

b.desc: Checking after every tool call that an agent's stated plan still matches what it actually just did, and flagging the first step where action and stated plan diverge.

a.desc: An evaluation run that scores as a success only because stale cached results from a previous run leaked into the harness — the agent did not actually perform the work in this run.

b.desc: A grader configuration bug where items that no judge can parse are silently marked correct instead of being flagged, inflating scores with items that were never actually judged.

a.desc: The shape of an agent's token spending across a task — whether the spend is front-loaded into early exploration, flat, or back-loaded into final verification — read as a profile curve over normalized task time.

b.desc: A scoring rubric rule requiring every judge criterion to cite the specific transcript line it is scored from, so that no criterion can be scored from overall impression.

a.desc: Freezing the menu of random seeds an evaluation samples from, so that re-runs draw exactly the same task variants and run-to-run differences cannot come from variant sampling.

b.desc: Counting how often an agent's final answer contradicts the output of a tool it itself called earlier in the same run — a per-run incidence of contradiction against its own evidence.
